trials.claim: Lifetime access to DivMagic on base plan
trials.claimQuote:
Lifetime access to DivMagic
- You must redeem your code(s) within 60 days of purchase
trials.reasoning: The binding terms let DivMagic modify the terms at any time and treat continued use as acceptance, which materially limits the promised lifetime access despite the one-payment marketing in E9.

exhibits.quote: DivMagic reserves the right to modify these Terms and Conditions at any time.
exhibits.argument: Vendor can unilaterally change terms at any time, undermining guaranteed lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: Your continued use of the extension constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.
exhibits.argument: Continued use forces acceptance of revised terms, so lifetime terms can be taken back.

exhibits.quote: No subscription. No renewals. One payment and it's yours.
exhibits.argument: The vendor states the Lifetime plan is a one-time payment with no subscription or renewals.

trials.reasoning: No admitted exhibits were provided about Plan 2's admin and user counts, so the claim cannot be checked either way.
No admitted exhibits were provided about Plan 10's admin and user counts, so the claim cannot be checked either way.

trials.reasoning: The binding terms allow DivMagic to modify the terms at any time effective on posting, which materially limits the promise of all future Lifetime Access Plan updates despite the marketing in E10.

exhibits.quote: DivMagic reserves the right to modify these Terms and Conditions at any time.
exhibits.argument: Vendor can modify terms anytime, voiding promise of all future updates.

exhibits.quote: Any changes will be effective upon posting the updated terms on our website.
exhibits.argument: Changes take effect on posting alone, allowing removal of promised future updates.

exhibits.quote:
✓All future updates, forever

✓Chrome, Firefox & all Chromium browsers

✓Use on 2 devices
exhibits.argument: The vendor lists all future updates forever as included with the Lifetime plan.

trials.claim: Base plan regular price stated as $300, sale price $49
trials.claimQuote:
Lifetime Access: $49 (was $300)
- Lifetime access to DivMagic
- You must redeem your code(s) within 60 days of purchase
trials.reasoning: The vendor site advertises saving $145 and 42% off lifetime access, which conflicts with the claimed $300 regular price reduced to $49, a $251 or about 84% saving.

exhibits.quote: Limited time:Save $145on lifetime access→See our prices to get DivMagic with discounts!
exhibits.argument: Official site advertises $145 saving, not $251 saving implied by $300 to $49.

exhibits.quote: Get DivMagic for 42% off Limited time deal for 22:45
exhibits.argument: Official discount is 42% off, inconsistent with ~84% off implied by $300 to $49.

trials.claim: Can copy design from any website and code of any web element with one click, including format conversion
trials.claimQuote: Copy design from any website, copy code of any web element with one click, and even convert formats
trials.reasoning: A buyer reports full-page copying loses styles, fonts, colors and designs, and the terms prohibit copying designs you do not own or have permission to use, materially limiting the claim of copying from any website despite the vendor's one-click and conversion marketing.

exhibits.quote: Copying a full page produces one text line of text in black and white -- a far cry from what you would expect with true styles, fonts, colors, and designs.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports full-page copy fails to reproduce styles, fonts, colors and designs.

exhibits.quote: Users should not copy, steal, or otherwise misuse designs or any intellectual property they do not own or have permission to use.
exhibits.argument: Vendor terms prohibit copying designs you do not own, contradicting copy from any website.

exhibits.quote: Hover over anything on any website and copy its HTML or CSS in one click. No DevTools, no guessing, just the code, ready to use.
exhibits.argument: The vendor confirms one-click copying of code from any website element.

exhibits.quote: Paste raw CSS, get Tailwind classes back, and colors included. Works even if the source site doesn't use Tailwind at all.
exhibits.argument: The vendor confirms format conversion from CSS to Tailwind.
